subject: VAPA
title: Visual Art I
description: Visual Art I is a foundational studio course covering drawing, perspective, color theory and painting, printmaking, design, sculpture and clay, portraiture, photography, collage, and digital art. Each unit pairs hands-on work with study of artists from many cultures and the critique process. The year ends with a personal body of work, an artist statement, and a curated home or community exhibition.
framework: 2019 California Arts Standards for Public Schools (Visual Arts, High School Proficient); 2020 CA Arts Education Framework

standards.VA:Cr1.1.HSI: Use multiple approaches to begin creative endeavors.
standards.VA:Cr1.2.HSI: Shape an artistic investigation of an aspect of present-day life using a contemporary practice of art or design.
standards.VA:Cr2.1.HSI: Engage in making a work of art or design without having a preconceived plan; experiment with materials and approaches.
standards.VA:Cr2.2.HSI: Explain how traditional and nontraditional materials may impact human health and the environment, and demonstrate safe handling of materials, tools, and equipment.
standards.VA:Cr2.3.HSI: Collaboratively develop a proposal for an installation, artwork, or space design that transforms the perception and experience of a particular place.
standards.VA:Cr3.1.HSI: Apply relevant criteria from traditional and contemporary cultural contexts to examine, reflect on, and plan revisions for works of art in progress.
standards.VA:Pr4.1.HSI: Analyze, select, and curate artifacts and/or artworks for presentation and preservation.
standards.VA:Pr5.1.HSI: Analyze and evaluate the reasons and ways an exhibition is presented.
standards.VA:Pr6.1.HSI: Analyze and describe the impact that an exhibition or collection has on personal awareness of social, cultural, or political beliefs.
standards.VA:Re7.1.HSI: Hypothesize ways in which art influences perception and understanding of human experiences.
standards.VA:Re7.2.HSI: Analyze how one's understanding of the world is affected by experiencing visual imagery.
standards.VA:Re8.1.HSI: Interpret an artwork or collection of works, supported by relevant and sufficient evidence found in the work and its various contexts.
standards.VA:Re9.1.HSI: Establish relevant criteria in order to evaluate a work of art or collection of works.
standards.VA:Cn10.1.HSI: Document the process of developing ideas from early stages to fully elaborated ideas.
standards.VA:Cn11.1.HSI: Describe how knowledge of culture, traditions, and history may influence personal responses to art.

units.title: Drawing Foundations: Line, Shape, and Value
units.big_idea: Drawing is a way of seeing; line and value turn flat paper into form.

units.title: Space and Perspective
units.big_idea: Artists create the illusion of depth with perspective systems, overlap, and atmosphere.

units.title: Color Theory and Painting
units.big_idea: Color relationships create mood, light, and harmony; painting media each have their own behaviors.

units.title: Principles of Design and Printmaking
units.big_idea: Principles of design organize the elements; printmaking multiplies an image and has a long history as public art.

units.title: Three-Dimensional Art and Sculpture
units.big_idea: Sculpture and installation change how we experience space and place.

units.title: Portraiture and the Figure
units.big_idea: Portraits reveal identity through proportion, expression, and symbol.

units.title: Photography, Collage, and Mixed Media
units.big_idea: Photography and collage let artists reframe everyday life and combine images into new meanings.

units.title: Personal Voice, Portfolio, and Exhibition
units.big_idea: Artists develop a body of work around a personal theme and share it through a curated exhibition.

objectives: Draw with contour and blind contour line

days.title: Sketchbook launch
days.work: Decorate a sketchbook cover with your name in three lettering styles and draw your non-dominant hand for 10 minutes.

days.title: Blind contour
days.work: Do five 3-minute blind contour drawings of a shoe, a plant, and your face in a mirror without looking at the paper.

days.title: Modified contour
days.work: Draw a kitchen utensil grouping with modified contour, glancing at the paper only at corners.

days.title: Cross-contour
days.work: Draw a banana and a crumpled paper bag using cross-contour lines to show form.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Select your best contour drawing and write a 5-sentence reflection on what improved during the week.

weeks.assessment: Sketchbook check for 10+ contour drawings and written reflection.

objectives: Use geometric and organic shapes to block in drawings

days.title: Shapes underneath
days.work: Block in a still life of three household objects using basic geometric shapes before refining edges.

days.title: Sighting and measuring
days.work: Learn pencil sighting to measure proportions; draw a chair accurately using sighting.

days.title: Gesture
days.work: Do 20 thirty-second gesture drawings of a family member doing household tasks or of figures in a sports video.

days.title: Negative space
days.work: Draw only the negative spaces around a chair or plant to correct shape errors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a 45-minute proportion drawing of a still life and self-check with sighting.

weeks.assessment: Proportion still life evaluated for accurate shapes and proportions.

days.title: Value scales
days.work: Create 9-step value scales with pencil blending, hatching, cross-hatching, and stippling.

days.title: Shading spheres
days.work: Render a sphere, cube, and cylinder with highlight, midtone, core shadow, reflected light, and cast shadow.

days.title: Light source lab
days.work: Photograph an egg under a single lamp from three angles and draw the best lighting.

days.title: Pen techniques
days.work: Shade the same egg in pen with hatching only.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Peer/parent critique comparing pencil and pen versions using the elements vocabulary.

weeks.assessment: Value scales and shaded forms checked against a rubric.

objectives: Compose and render a still life with a full value range
materials: still life objects (white objects work best)

days.title: Set up
days.work: Arrange 3–5 white objects under a strong lamp; make three thumbnail compositions and pick one.

days.title: Block-in
days.work: Lightly block in the composition with sighting.

days.title: Value
days.work: Lay in the darkest darks and lightest lights, then build midtones.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine edges, textures, and cast shadows.

days.title: Critique
days.work: Write criteria for a successful still life and use them to self-evaluate your drawing.

weeks.assessment: Still life drawing scored against self-written and teacher criteria.

days.title: Frottage
days.work: Make crayon rubbings of 10 textures around the house and label them.

days.title: Texture study
days.work: Draw close-up studies of tree bark, fabric, and metal.

days.title: Charcoal
days.work: Draw a crumpled paper bag in charcoal using subtractive eraser drawing.

days.title: Ink wash
days.work: Paint a quick ink-wash study of a houseplant with three dilutions.

days.title: Unit 1 portfolio review
days.work: Assemble your best three drawings and document your growth with photos and captions.

days.title: Perspective in art
days.work: Analyze Leonardo's "The Last Supper" and trace its orthogonals on a printout to find the vanishing point.

days.title: Boxes in space
days.work: Draw floating boxes above, below, and on the horizon line in one-point perspective.

days.title: Hallway
days.work: Draw a hallway or room interior in one-point perspective.

days.title: Street scene
days.work: Draw a one-point street scene with buildings, windows, and sidewalk.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Add value and details to the street scene.

weeks.assessment: One-point drawing assessed for correct convergence.

days.title: Two-point boxes
days.work: Draw boxes in two-point perspective at different heights.

days.title: Building
days.work: Draw your house or a local building in two-point.

days.title: Worm's/bird's-eye
days.work: Draw a box from a bird's-eye and worm's-eye view.

days.title: City block
days.work: Draw an imaginary city block in two-point perspective.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-critique perspective drawings with a checklist.

days.title: Chinese landscape painting
days.work: Study a Song dynasty landscape and identify how mist shows depth.

days.title: Plein air
days.work: Draw a landscape outdoors with foreground, middle ground, and background.

days.title: Value layers
days.work: Redo the landscape with value fading in the distance.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare Chinese and Hudson River School landscapes in writing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 2 review of perspective drawings.

materials: tempera or acrylic primaries plus white and black

days.title: Color wheel
days.work: Mix a 12-step color wheel from primaries.

days.title: Tints and shades
days.work: Create tint and shade scales for one color.

days.title: Color schemes
days.work: Paint four small squares in complementary, analogous, triadic, and monochromatic schemes.

days.title: Color and mood
days.work: Analyze how Picasso's Blue Period paintings use color for mood.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Color theory quiz.

days.title: Material safety
days.work: Learn safe handling and cleanup of paints and brushes, including not pouring pigments down storm drains.

days.title: Technique sampler
days.work: Paint a sampler grid of wet-on-wet, gradient wash, glazing, salt, lifting, and wax resist.

days.title: Sky study
days.work: Paint three sky studies at different times of day.

days.title: Botanical
days.work: Paint a leaf or flower from observation with glazing.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label the sampler and choose the technique you will use in the landscape.

days.title: Impressionism
days.work: Study Monet's "Haystacks" series and explain how light changes color.

days.title: Thumbnails
days.work: Paint 3 small studies of the same view at different times of day.

days.title: Painting
days.work: Start a landscape painting in broken color.

days.title: Finishing
days.work: Finish the landscape painting.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an interpretation of a Monet painting citing visual evidence.

days.title: Fauvism
days.work: Analyze Matisse's "Woman with a Hat" and list arbitrary colors.

days.title: Expressionism
days.work: Analyze Munch's "The Scream" and Kirchner's street scenes.

days.title: Expressive painting
days.work: Paint a familiar place in arbitrary colors to express a mood.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish the painting and title it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short artist statement explaining color choices.

days.title: Feldman critique
days.work: Learn describe–analyze–interpret–judge and critique a Frida Kahlo painting.

days.title: Self-critique
days.work: Critique your two paintings with the same method.

days.title: Revise
days.work: Revise one painting based on critique.

days.title: Photograph
days.work: Photograph and document work.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Unit 3 portfolio check.

days.title: Principles hunt
days.work: Find magazine examples of each principle of design and make a reference sheet.

days.title: Balance
days.work: Create symmetrical, asymmetrical, and radial balance compositions with cut paper.

days.title: Emphasis
days.work: Make a composition that uses contrast to create a focal point.

days.title: Rhythm
days.work: Create a rhythm/pattern design.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Principles quiz.

days.title: Hokusai
days.work: Study Hokusai's "The Great Wave" and ukiyo-e woodblock printing.

days.title: Posada and the Taller de Gráfica Popular
days.work: Study José Guadalupe Posada's calaveras and Mexican political prints.

days.title: Design
days.work: Draw 3 thumbnails for a print about your community, thinking in black and white shapes.

days.title: Transfer
days.work: Transfer the design in reverse to a foam plate.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how printmaking was used as public art.

materials: carving tools or pencil for foam

days.title: Carving safety
days.work: Learn tool safety (carve away from hands).

days.title: Carve
days.work: Carve or press the plate.

days.title: Proof
days.work: Pull a proof print and adjust.

days.title: Edition
days.work: Print an edition of 5 prints, numbering and signing correctly.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Select the best print and critique.

objectives: Apply principles of design to a poster with text and image
materials: poster board or free design app
Library of Congress WPA poster images

days.title: WPA posters
days.work: Analyze five 1930s WPA posters from the Library of Congress and note how each uses hierarchy, color, and lettering.

days.title: Thumbnails
days.work: Sketch six thumbnails for a poster promoting a real community event (library program, farmers market, park cleanup).

days.title: Lettering
days.work: Practice hand-lettering the title in two styles and choose one that matches the event's mood.

days.title: Final poster
days.work: Produce the final 11x17 poster using a limited palette of three colors.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Get feedback from someone who didn't see it in progress: can they find the event, date, and place in 5 seconds?

weeks.assessment: Poster evaluated on hierarchy, readability, and design principles.

days.title: Select
days.work: Lay out all semester work and select six pieces that show range (drawing, perspective, painting, print, design).

days.title: Document
days.work: Photograph each piece squarely in natural light with a neutral backdrop and crop/label the files.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a 100-word reflection for each piece: goal, process, what you'd change.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the portfolio to family, explaining one piece in depth with a Feldman-style critique.

days.title: Goal setting
days.work: Compare your week 1 contour drawing to a recent drawing and write three goals for semester 2.

objectives: Explore positive and negative space in sculpture

days.title: Sculpture survey
days.work: Compare Michelangelo's "David", Barbara Hepworth's pierced forms, and Ruth Asawa's wire sculptures; note how each uses space.

days.title: Paper techniques
days.work: Practice scoring, folding, curling, tabbing, and slotting cardstock in a technique sampler.

days.title: Abstract sculpture
days.work: Build a freestanding abstract paper sculpture at least 10 inches tall that is interesting from every side.

days.title: Lighting
days.work: Photograph the sculpture with a lamp from three angles and note how shadows change the form.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Critique the sculpture for balance, unity, and use of negative space.

objectives: Use pinch, coil, and slab methods

days.title: Clay safety
days.work: Learn clay safety (wet cleanup to avoid silica dust) and wedge clay.

days.title: Pinch pot
days.work: Make a pinch pot with even walls.

days.title: Coil
days.work: Build a coil vessel using score and slip.

days.title: Slab
days.work: Construct a slab box with a lid.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare the three methods in a written reflection and choose one for the final project.

weeks.topic: Clay project: functional or sculptural vessel
objectives: Design and build a ceramic piece inspired by a cultural tradition

days.title: Inspiration
days.work: Study Pueblo pottery by Maria Martinez and Japanese Jomon pottery; sketch surface designs.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build the vessel or sculpture using your chosen method.

days.title: Surface
days.work: Add texture or sgraffito designs at the leather-hard stage.

days.title: Paint and seal
days.work: After drying, paint and seal the piece.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an artist statement explaining your cultural inspiration.

objectives: Propose an installation that transforms a space

days.title: Installation art
days.work: Study Christo and Jeanne-Claude's "Running Fence" (Sonoma/Marin, 1976) and Yayoi Kusama's infinity rooms.

days.title: Site study
days.work: Choose a space (yard, hallway, park) and photograph and measure it.

days.title: Proposal
days.work: Collaborate with a sibling or friend to sketch a proposal that transforms the space.

days.title: Model
days.work: Build a scale model in a shoebox.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the proposal and model and explain how it changes a viewer's experience.

objectives: Draw the face with correct proportions

days.title: Proportion guide
days.work: Learn standard facial proportions (eyes halfway, etc.) and draw a front-view guide.

days.title: Eyes and nose
days.work: Draw 6 studies of eyes and noses from a mirror.

days.title: Mouth and ears
days.work: Draw studies of mouths and ears.

days.title: Full face
days.work: Draw a family member's face from life using the guide.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare to a photo and correct proportions.

objectives: Create a self-portrait that expresses identity

days.title: Self-portrait history
days.work: Compare self-portraits by Rembrandt, Frida Kahlo, and Kehinde Wiley and note symbols they use.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Sketch thumbnails including 3 personal symbols.

days.title: Draw
days.work: Draw the self-portrait from a mirror.

days.title: Render
days.work: Add value or color and the symbols.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation of your symbols.

objectives: Draw the human figure in proportion

days.title: Figure proportions
days.work: Learn the 7.5-heads rule and draw a proportion chart.

days.title: Gesture
days.work: Do 20 one-minute gestures of a family member posing.

days.title: Contrapposto
days.work: Study the Greek "Doryphoros" and draw a contrapposto pose.

days.title: Long pose
days.work: Draw a 30-minute seated figure from life.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Critique proportion with a partner.

days.title: Egyptian and Roman
days.work: Compare Fayum mummy portraits with Egyptian pharaoh portraits.

days.title: Benin and Mughal
days.work: Study Benin bronze heads and Mughal miniature portraits.

days.title: Modern
days.work: Study Amedeo Modigliani and Alice Neel.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Write a comparison of two portraits from different cultures citing visual evidence.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on portrait traditions.

objectives: Create a portrait of someone in your community

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview your subject and photograph them in a meaningful setting.

days.title: Sketch
days.work: Make a composition sketch including setting objects.

days.title: Create
days.work: Begin the final portrait.

days.title: Finish
days.work: Finish the portrait.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the portrait to the subject and record their reaction.

days.title: Photo history
days.work: Compare Dorothea Lange's "Migrant Mother" and Ansel Adams's Yosemite photographs; note composition and purpose.

days.title: Composition challenge
days.work: Shoot 10 photos each demonstrating rule of thirds, leading lines, framing, symmetry, and pattern.

days.title: Light study
days.work: Photograph the same object at morning, noon, and golden hour and describe the differences.

days.title: Edit
days.work: Edit your best five photos for crop, exposure, and black-and-white conversion in a free editing app.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present a 5-photo contact sheet labeled with the technique each shows.

objectives: Tell a story through a photo series

days.title: Documentary photography
days.work: Study Gordon Parks's photo essays and how sequence creates narrative.

days.title: Plan
days.work: Choose a subject in your community (a market, a family recipe, a local business) and write a shot list.

days.title: Shoot
days.work: Shoot 50+ photos following the shot list and permission guidelines.

days.title: Edit and sequence
days.work: Select and sequence 8 photos and write captions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the photo essay and explain your sequencing choices.

objectives: Create a mixed-media collage that combines images into new meaning

days.title: Romare Bearden
days.work: Study Bearden's collages of Harlem life and Hannah Höch's photomontage.

days.title: Gather
days.work: Gather images, textures, and papers around a theme (home, memory, the future).

days.title: Compose
days.work: Experiment with arrangements without gluing; photograph three options.

days.title: Build
days.work: Glue down and add paint and drawing to unify the collage.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an interpretation of a classmate's or sibling's collage, then your own.

materials: free app (e.g., Krita or a browser-based editor)

days.title: Digital tools
days.work: Learn layers, brushes, selection, and opacity in a free app.

days.title: Digital copy
days.work: Recreate one of your earlier drawings digitally to learn the tools.

days.title: Original
days.work: Create an original digital illustration combining a photo and drawing.

days.title: Refine
days.work: Refine color and layer effects.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare digital vs. traditional workflows in a short reflection.

weeks.topic: Contemporary art and finding your theme
objectives: Choose a theme for a body of work

days.title: Contemporary artists
days.work: Explore work by Kara Walker, El Anatsui, Ai Weiwei, and Judy Baca and note their themes.

days.title: Artist research
days.work: Research one artist in depth and write a 400-word profile with images.

days.title: Mind map
days.work: Make a mind map of personal themes (family, place, nature, technology).

days.title: Proposal
days.work: Write a proposal for a 3-piece body of work with media and sketches.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Conference on the proposal and revise.

days.title: Piece 1 start
days.work: Begin piece 1, documenting process with photos.

days.title: Piece 1 finish
days.work: Finish piece 1 and write process notes.

days.title: Piece 2 start
days.work: Begin piece 2 with a variation on the theme.

days.title: Piece 2 finish
days.work: Finish piece 2.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Mid-project critique using your criteria.

weeks.assessment: Two finished pieces with process documentation.

weeks.topic: Body of work: piece 3 and artist statement

days.title: Piece 3
days.work: Create piece 3, completing the series.

days.title: Refinement
days.work: Revise any of the three pieces based on critique.

days.title: Artist statement
days.work: Draft a 250-word artist statement explaining theme, media, and process.

days.title: Revise statement
days.work: Revise the statement for clarity and specific language.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Self-evaluate the series with criteria you established.

days.title: Exhibitions
days.work: Take a virtual tour of a museum exhibition and analyze how works are grouped, labeled, and lit.

days.title: Select
days.work: Select 10–12 works from the year for your exhibition, including the series.

days.title: Labels
days.work: Write wall labels with title, medium, date, and a one-sentence description.

days.title: Install
days.work: Install the exhibition in your home or a community space, considering flow and lighting.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Walk through the show and adjust placement.

days.title: Opening
days.work: Host an exhibition opening for family and friends; give a short talk.

days.title: Audience feedback
days.work: Collect feedback in a guest book and summarize responses.

days.title: Impact reflection
days.work: Write about how visiting a real or virtual exhibition this year changed your view of a social or cultural issue.

days.title: Digital portfolio
days.work: Create a digital portfolio of the year's best work with captions.

days.title: Final reflection
days.work: Write a final reflection on growth and goals for next year's art course.
